newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans tumble, November hits four-month low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans tumble, November hits four-month low.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures tumbled on Tuesday and the November contract fell to its lowest level since January amid outlooks for ideal growing conditions in the U.S. Midwest, pit sources said.

"It was largely a fund-led selloff today," said Mark Weidner, oilseeds analyst with Cargill Investor Services. "Weather had a lot to do with it and plantings progress kept the support away from the market."
Weidner and others predicted USDA's weekly crop progress report, due at 1500 CDT, would show between 70 and 80 percent of the crop was seeded.
"It may not be a record pace but it won't be very far off of it," Weidner said, referring to seeding progress.
Early-planted crops historically have yielded better than late-planted ones.

The July escaped the selloff with light losses and traded firm most of the session on bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections data. USDA put inspections at 11.5 million bushels, above expectations for five million to 10 million.
Soybeans ended 4-3/4 to 13-1/2 cents a bushel lower with July down 4-3/4 at $8.31-1/4 and new crop November down 12-1/2 cents at $6.65.
Old crop July rallied to $8.44-1/2 near midday on ideas prices had fallen enough to attract more world buying interest, as evidenced by USDA's export inspections data.
Nearby contracts have been sensitive to the export data in recent weeks amid ideas USDA would further trim its already tight ending stocks forecast of 125 million bushels.

USDA in May put U.S. soy exports at 895 million bushels for the marketing year ending August 31. Inspections were at 782 million bushels as of May 22, versus 691 million at this time last year. The pace led some analysts to predict USDA will raise its export estimate in the next crop report.
But some suggested the moves were tied more to technical indicators than fundamental signs.
"The inspects were good but for the July to gain and the August not move with it indicates it was more of a technical thing rather than fundamental," Weidner said.

On the day, funds sold at least 10 million bushels, led by Smith Barney. Smith Barney sold five million bushels August and one million July. Merrill Lynch sold three million July and two million August, and Refco Inc sold 3.5 million July and 1.5 million November.
Commercials were buyers on the day with Cargill Inc accounting for 3.2 million bushels November.
In spread action, Tenco Inc spread one million bushels July/November at $1.61 to $1.63-1/2, premium July. The spread tacked on 7-3/4 cents to close at $1.66-1/4.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 70,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 63,364 contracts.
